name: smjob filter help
purpose: Print the same job-tracker filter help through its registered alias.
side_effects_assessment: Alias uses the same print-only handler as sm_dispatch_job filter help; no filter state is changed. Normal output buffering/interpreter bookkeeping occurs.

help_strings.text:
This udw command enables filtering the output of the job tracker for specified SUID(s).

usage: sm_dispatch_job filter [action] SUID

Available actions:
  1) disable -> Allow job tracking output for the specified SUID
  2) enable  -> Suppress job tracking output for the specified SUID
  3) except  -> Suppress job tracking output for all but the specifed SUID
  4) only    -> Allow job tracking output for only the specified SUID
  5) show    -> Display filtering status for the specified SUID
                If called without a SUID, displays filtering status for all

purpose: Show image-pipeline history; retail per-record formatting is compiled out.
review: No args supplies zero to A01C95FC, which defaults to 200 records. Reads 209E3038 history index, does modulo arithmetic and calls A01C964C (BX LR) for each slot; no target mutation. Optional numeric count uses strtol but large counts are unnecessary; use no args only.

purpose: Probe current buffer debug view; expected return 0 only.

purpose: Probe advertised circular-buffer diagnostic if dynamically registered.

purpose: Print image-pipeline LMB state and counters.

name: firm.query_value_suid
purpose: Read current and compiled values for one physically established numeric firmware group.
argument_syntax: SUID (13-bit unsigned group ID), not a packed item ID
side_effects_assessment: Existing local registry/data reads and UART output only.

review.proof: Masks input to 13 bits, resolves registered SUID, loops 0..descriptor maximum, gets current value using actual SUID and index, prints current/default/name in 100-byte row buffer with byte99 NUL. All known name lengths fit even two signed32 minima.
review.data_quality: One group per UART line. Largest group may exceed conservative 4KB transport guideline; validate exact expected item identities and full-row delimiters before calling complete. No whole-table retry.

name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_counters
purpose: Read the WiFi SDIO command, transfer, timeout and error counters without clearing them.
review_evidence: A0454F76 checks card availability, calls vtable +0x14 with port 0 and a 40-byte stack buffer, and prints only on interface result 1. Resolved A03C0882 -> A03C67C0 -> A03C129A copies ten words from driver object +0x3c4 into that buffer; no counter reset or card transaction.
side_effects_assessment: Cached RAM reads, stack writes and UART output. Counters remain untouched by the getter.

name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_caps
purpose: Read the SDIO manufacturer/device IDs, function capabilities, block sizes, and speed support needed by the emulator.
review_evidence: A0454796 sends request 0x65 into a 0xac-byte stack structure, then request 0x64 into the same request output. Resolved A03C668E queues to A03C69C4; 0x65 selects A03C6D14, which copies cached CCCR/FBR and manufacturer/device fields via A03C130E/A03C1322/A03C12D6; 0x64 selects A03C6A66, which copies cached function count and function sizes via A03C138E/A03C13A0/A03C13A4. Formatting runs only after successful request completion.
side_effects_assessment: Two serialized driver requests, semaphore/queue bookkeeping, cached RAM reads, caller-buffer writes and UART output. These selectors do not issue discovery, configuration, radio connection, reset or nonvolatile writes.
result_limitations: The helper waits for request completion internally; host timeout is a capture bound, not a guarantee that every firmware fault is bounded. These fields are cached capability values, not a new card enumeration.

name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_status
purpose: Read and dump the current 32 bytes at SDIO function 0 offsets 0x00..0x1f.
review_evidence: A04546C4 -> resolved vtable +0x20 A03C08A2 -> A03C6816 -> A03C4BD8. Last helper invokes A03C506C with direction 0, function 0, address 0, length 0x20 and a stack output buffer. A03C52E4 loops over exactly 32 bytes using A03C13DC. A045EE36 prints the successful read as hex.
side_effects_assessment: 32 SDIO read transactions and normal controller/request bookkeeping; this will increment the SDIO counters. No write request to card configuration, connection, scan, or persistent settings is selected.
result_limitations: CCCR registers are live, so compare to the cached capability dump without assuming atomicity. Handler success alone is weak: A03C6816 returns 1 after its helper even if that helper prints a read failure; require the 32-byte dump.

name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_counters
purpose: Read counters after the 32 status-byte reads to measure actual SDIO activity.
review_evidence: A0454F76 checks card availability, calls vtable +0x14 with port 0 and a 40-byte stack buffer, and prints only on interface result 1. Resolved A03C0882 -> A03C67C0 -> A03C129A copies ten words from driver object +0x3c4 into that buffer; no counter reset or card transaction.
side_effects_assessment: Cached RAM reads, stack writes and UART output. Counters remain untouched by the getter.

name: ultra_spectra.get_iovar
purpose: Read the WiFi driver integer variable mpc.
review_evidence: A0453F3A consumes one bounded string (100-byte input buffer). A0459322 checks the driver pointer, calls A0459414 with no input payload and 4-byte output, and prints only on success. A0459414 passes ioctl 0x106 through getter A0459568 (vtable +0x0c), while setters use 0x107 through A045955C. The selected variable names occur in this firmware: mpc at A04585B8, nmode at A062303C. The corresponding getter output is interpreted as a little-endian 32-bit integer by A0459656.
side_effects_assessment: A driver GET_VAR request with a variable name only, stack buffers, transaction bookkeeping and UART output. No setter payload or nonvolatile configuration path is selected.
result_limitations: The radio firmware can reject unsupported variables. An empty result with a normal prompt is not a successful value read. Do not use this integer handler for strings such as ver or for secret material.

name: ultra_spectra.test_endian
purpose: Record the compiled 16/32/64-bit endian conversion test vectors for emulator comparison.
review_evidence: A045520A..A045527E prints twelve literal vectors through A0453EEE and returns; all values are fixed immediates/literals (0x0102, 0x01020304, 0x0102030405060708 and their reversed-byte counterparts). There is no hardware access.
side_effects_assessment: UART output and stack/formatting bookkeeping only.
result_limitations: These are compiled fixed-vector outputs. They are not evidence that the physical SDIO bus exercised all endian cases.

name: webfwupdate.get_base_md
purpose: Read the 16-byte base firmware digest and any matching base_md entry in local secure configuration.
review_evidence: A0470EEA reads 16 bytes from the existing base-MD pointer at 20E09780 and formats 32 hex characters via A046ED8A. It then requests section web_product_update/key base_md with a 65-byte output buffer through A03C8882/A03C8696. The secure-configuration helper seeks and reads existing cached file descriptors; it never selects a file write. Missing entry is skipped because caller passed a NULL default.
side_effects_assessment: Local metadata reads and UART output. Secure-config lookup uses its mutex and changes file positions; on bad/stale file reads it can close those cached handles and compact the in-memory descriptor list. No firmware update, download, or nonvolatile write.
result_limitations: The base digest pointer is initialized by the firmware lifecycle; unlike the formatted optional configuration entry it is not null-checked by this handler. Established running firmware is the precondition. This command does not recompute the digest.

name: heapmgr log block
argument_syntax: lookup flags=0, key high word=16777216 (0x01000000), key low word=1
purpose: Read allocator purgeability, lock flag, client/priority fields, pin count and size for the existing root-directory block.
control_flow_proof: A016098E..09AA reads three decimal uint32 words via A01612B8, then A01608F2 copies them to a 12-byte stack key and calls A0160802 with display_filter=0. Exact words 0,16777216,1 select name lookup of the existing root-directory key 0100000000000001; they are not raw addresses.

A0160802..089A calls A015FB5A six times with selectors1,3,2,5,6,7, each output pointing into its own stack. Selector0/4 and all property setters are unreachable. It formats one bounded metadata line and waits one RTOS tick.

A015FB5A -> A015F884: leading key flag is0, so only name-lookup branch A015FCF4 executes. A015FCF4 hashes eight key bytes with A015FB80 -> A000723C CRC and standard remainder trampoline A0025294, reads one of211 initialized buckets, and traverses existing links. A015FBF2 -> A0160D36 -> A015F3D6 resolves an existing descriptor and A016005A copies eight bytes to a local key buffer; A0010550 compares exactly eight bytes. A015FB92 -> A0160D36 -> A016007E reads the next existing link. No hash insert/remove or allocator path is reachable.

On a key match A0160D48 reads descriptor generation into caller-local storage. A0160D1A -> A0160C60 -> A015F3D6 checks index, non-null header and generation, then reads the existing header pointer. The successful branch was physically exercised for this exact key by ram.block_info in physical61, and the whole hash index was captured in physical58 (8 entries, this block index1 in bucket118).

A0160004 reads selected header fields: selector1=byte26 bit0 purgeable, selector3=byte24 client/major priority field, selector2=byte25 minor priority, selector5=word8 size, selector6=byte27 pin/use count, selector7=byte26 bit1 lock. Its only writes are to each caller-provided stack output.

A0161270 formats into a256-byte stack buffer, gets length, and calls provider vtable+24. Physical57 resolves 20943A40 -> A061F594 -> A061F598; +24=A0431A59 -> A02C2A7A UART writer; parser+10=A0431979 -> A02C3DE2 decimal parser. The fixed line format and integer arguments fit the formatting buffer.

A02F6D70(1) checks scheduler state through A02F7144 and invokes the established RTOS delay A04E6650. This updates volatile current-thread delay/scheduler counters for one tick and returns; it does not access storage or command actuators. This delay path is already used by captured heap tree diagnostics.
side_effects_assessment: UART output, parser/formatter stack storage and a one-tick RTOS scheduling delay. No allocator mutation, file write, persistent setting or actuator operation.
output_limits: Exactly one metadata line from6 property reads. Hash walks existing finite chain; prior complete capture has8 entries. Existing-key lookup errors are not checked by the formatter, so raw output must be cross-validated against the known header rather than assuming any prompt means valid data.

If overrides are permitted, only the fixed scalar DSID0x13FC3 is read usingA03211B4 (bounded current-task cache, otherwise storage getter); there is no transaction unlock or write path. Earlier DS2 returned0 for that override, which is retained as raw evidence because zero alone is ambiguous. When no nonzero override is returned, A03237B6 reads20D02D94. Physical68 proves it is nonzero20180624, so the fallback-provider call and cache write are skipped on the observed state.
